newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sells 8.988 bln reais in Treasury papers.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sells 8.988 bln reais in Treasury papers.

text.p: Brazil's central bank, on behalf of the National Treasury, raised 8.988 billion reais in an auction of notes and letters, dealers said on Monday.
A total of 6.324 billion reais was sold in two series of National Treasury letters known as LTNs.

A total of 4.093 billion reais of 183-day LTNs, due October 1, 1997, was sold at an overnight call money rate of 2.221 percent a month. The central bank also sold 2.231 billion reais of 365-day LTNs, due in April 1, 1998, at a call money rate of 2.254 percent a month.
A total of 1.439 billion reais was sold in two series of dollar-indexed National Treasury notes (NTN-D).

The bank sold 733 million reais of NTN-D notes, which are due on April 1, 1999, and pay an annual yield of 10.86 percent. The bank also sold 706 million reais of NTN-D notes coming due April 1, 2000, paying an annual yield of 10.85 percent.

Some 1.225 billion reais were sold in National Treasury notes (NTN) indexed to the variation of Brazil's reference rate (TR). The notes, which are due in October 1, 1997, pay annual yields of 12.64 percent plus the variation of the TR in the maturity period.
